title: CM-CNN-Accel: Microarchitecture-Aware Spatial and Temporal Computation Skipping for CNN Inference on AVX-512 CPUs
description:
Reference implementations, AVX-512 kernels, benchmark drivers and result files for the technical report CM-CNN-Accel: Microarchitecture-Aware Spatial and Temporal Computation Skipping for CNN Inference on AVX-512 CPUs (version 2.0, November 2026).

The report asks which kinds of computation redundancy turn into wall-clock time on a general-purpose core, and identifies three coupled constraints: SIMD execution granularity, load-port throughput per FMA, and the convolution topology that fixes how much arithmetic one skipping decision controls.

Measured results on a single AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX core (Zen 5, AVX-512F/BW/DQ/VL/VNNI, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, g++ 16.2.1): the conv_tile dense microkernel reaches 0.5 load micro-ops per FMA and 81 GMAC/s, where scalar-gather sparse kernels need about 2.0 and lose time despite fewer MACs; 16-lane-aligned structured pruning over a union-find channel permutation gives 2.70x on ResNet-18 (+0.56pp accuracy) and 1.66-1.70x on MobileNetV2 (+1.39pp); VGG-4 on 78%-zero input with 8-lane co-activation clustering removes 84.14% of MACs at 4.33x and 95.00% accuracy; the P2 temporal scheme, with a dense in-place fallback above a 0.50 MAC-weighted dirty ratio, eliminates 51.3-75.4% of MACs on fixed-camera streams and 33.7-37.4% on hard cuts, and reproduces scene-cut frames bit-exactly. Numerically, max|dlogit| against PyTorch is 8.66e-4 on static images and 1.44e-3 over 216 real-video frames, with Top-1 agreement 0.995-1.000. The Tile Arithmetic Density Model alpha_l = MACs_l / (Tiles_l * C_in,l) ~= 4*C_out,l*K_l^2/g_l explains why the same video stream yields 1.80x for ResNet-50 while ShuffleNetV2-x0.5 loses 12% to scheduling overhead.

Contents: paper1_bundle/ (manuscript PDFs, Markdown source, figures, 14 result files), native/ (AVX-512 kernels), experiments/cm-cnn-*/ (drivers, datasets, per-phase results), src/lib/vision/ and src/__tests__/cm-cnn-*.test.ts (models, dataset generators, acceptance tests), scripts/ (dataset generation and PyTorch cross-checks), docs/CM_CNN_ACCELERATION.md, file/cm_cnn_accel_paper/. Files larger than 5 MB (exported weights, dataset streams) are not redistributed; paper1_bundle/08_PhaseE_Model_Export_SHA256.json and the per-phase weights.sha256 files pin their digests.

Reproduction: g++ -O3 -march=native -mavx512f -mavx512bw -mfma -std=c++20 native/cm_production_avx512.cpp -o experiments/cm-cnn-production/cm_production_avx512; acceptance tests run with node --test src/__tests__/cm-cnn-accel.test.ts on Node 22 or newer.
notes: Dataset and corpus licences: none of the evaluation corpora are redistributed here. Model weights (torchvision and exported .bin files) are not redistributed; digests are recorded in paper1_bundle/08_PhaseE_Model_Export_SHA256.json and the per-phase weights.sha256 files. Real-video frames are not redistributed either; data/real_videos/ holds manifests only. Code is released under MPL-2.0.
